summary: Fremont NF pass in Lake County where a patrol lookout was often used around 1910; no built structure is described, and most vehicles can reach it today.

access.note: Accessible to most vehicles, according to the ONDA guide to the Fremont.

visit.trail_note: Walkers can head either direction on the Fremont National Recreation Trail and the Oregon Desert Trail.

events.note: c.1910: a point where a patrol lookout was frequently used by the ranger stationed at the Paisley Ranger Station. No structure is described.

evidence.supports: c.1910 point where a patrol lookout was frequently used; Paisley ranger
evidence.quote: A point where a patrol lookout was frequently used by the Ranger stationed at the Paisley Ranger Station.

evidence.supports: Entry drawn from early ranger diaries in the forest archives
evidence.quote: Early Ranger Diaries, Fremont National Forest Archives

evidence.supports: Most vehicles can reach the pass; walkers can go either direction on the Fremont trail and ODT
evidence.quote: Avery Pass and Morgan Butte are also accessible to most vehicles, where you can walk in either direction and enjoy some time on the Fremont National Recreation Trail and ODT.

evidence.supports: Morgan Butte is one of a few remaining staffed fire lookout towers; also reachable by most vehicles
evidence.quote: The Morgan Butte lookout is one of a few remaining staffed fire lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Only a one-line directory note (c.1910) and a recreation guide exist. No source describes a built lookout structure at Avery Pass, so the record's kind and status may need checking; this may be a point rather than a tower. The Oregon Lookouts entry is undated beyond c.1910. The Fremont forest history PDF names no Avery Pass lookout (its only Avery match is a person's name). Access rests on the ONDA guide, not an agency page; check the Paisley Ranger District before a visitor relies on it. The brief's access and status were 'unknown'; no change proposed.
